issues.legal_issue: An application to extend the time for payment or rescind a contract after a decree for specific performance may be entertained by the court of first instance when the appellate decree arose in the same suit, but it must be dealt with on the original side rather than as an execution proceeding.
material_facts: The appellate court granted a decree for specific performance and fixed a time for payment of the balance consideration.
The judgment-debtor applied for rescission under Section 28 while execution was proceeding in the court where the original suit had been filed.
The High Court rejected the application as not maintainable on the execution side.
issues.conclusion: The application was maintainable in the court of first instance because the appellate decree was part of the same suit, but it should have been treated as an interlocutory application on the original side and decided according to law, rather than dismissed merely because it was filed on the execution side.
issues.legal_principle: Section 28(1) of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 requires an application for extension of time or rescission to be made in the same suit. Under Section 37 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the court of first instance is included as the court that passed an appellate decree for execution purposes; an appeal is a continuation of the suit. The court retains control over a decree for specific performance after it is passed. Procedure should be moulded to serve substantial justice unless it concerns jurisdiction. The Court approved Maruti Vishnu Kshirsagar v. Bapu Keshav Jadhav, rejected Ibrahim Shariff v. Masthan Shariff, and relied on K. Kalpana Saraswathi v. P.S.S. Somasundaram Chettiar.

rule.if: specific_performance_proceeding and appellate_decree_in_same_suit and original_suit_and_execution_in_same_court and application_filed_on_execution_side

predicates.specific_performance_proceeding: The proceeding concerns a decree for specific performance of a contract for the sale or lease of immovable property.
predicates.appellate_decree_in_same_suit: An appellate court granted the decree for specific performance in the same suit in which the original court had acted.
predicates.original_suit_and_execution_in_same_cour: The original suit and the execution proceeding are before the same court of first instance.
predicates.application_filed_on_execution_side: A party filed an application for extension of time or rescission as part of the execution proceeding rather than on the original side.

issues.definition: When a specific-performance decree is granted on appeal in the same suit and the original suit and execution are before the same court, an application filed on the execution side is maintainable in that court but must be dealt with on the original side.

issues.legal_issue: The Supreme Court may decline to interfere with a lower court’s erroneous procedural dismissal of an application when the circumstances do not warrant appellate intervention.
material_facts: The decree for specific performance had become final.
The balance consideration was deposited while a second appeal was pending.
No steps had been taken to bring the alleged default in timely payment to the High Court’s attention.
The decree-holder had been in possession of the land for a long time, and execution was midway.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to interfere under Article 136, dismissed the appeal without costs, and allowed the application to lie in quietus where it had been filed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied its discretionary power under Article 136 of the Constitution, concluding that the circumstances did not call for interference despite the High Court’s error in dismissing the application on procedural grounds. No earlier case was relied on for this conclusion.

rule.if: appeal_to_supreme_court_against_procedural_dismissal and decree_for_specific_performance_final and payment_made_during_further_appeal and alleged_default_not_brought_to_appellate_court and decree_holder_in_long_possession and execution_underway

predicates.appeal_to_supreme_court_against_procedur: A party appeals to the Supreme Court after a lower court has dismissed an application on procedural grounds.
predicates.decree_for_specific_performance_final: The decree granting specific performance has become final.
predicates.payment_made_during_further_appeal: The balance consideration was paid while a further appeal was pending.
predicates.alleged_default_not_brought_to_appellate: No steps were taken to bring the alleged payment default to the attention of the court hearing the further appeal.
predicates.decree_holder_in_long_possession: The decree-holder had been in possession of the property for a long time.
predicates.execution_underway: Execution of the decree had already begun and was midway.

issues.definition: When a procedural dismissal is appealed to the Supreme Court and the decree is final, payment was made during a further appeal, the alleged default was not brought to that court, the decree-holder had long possession, and execution was underway, the Supreme Court may decline interference and dismiss the appeal.
